About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Global Supply Management Team

The Global Supply Management Team ensures that Zipline has the parts it needs from suppliers around the world in a reliable, sustainable, and cost-effective way. We build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, negotiate contracts, and monitor supplier performance to reduce supply risk. The team also works closely with the design engineering, supplier industrial engineering, finance, program management, and material management teams to understand part design, manage supply against demand, drive cost reductions, and streamline logistics across international markets.

The Role

As a Global Supply Management Intern, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the systems, data, and supplier relationships that power Zipline’s global supply chain. You’ll work alongside supply managers, engineers, finance, and operations teams to support sourcing, analytics, and day-to-day execution. This role is perfect for a student to apply classroom knowledge to real-world challenges in procurement, logistics, and global operations.

Your work will directly support Zipline’s mission to deliver essential goods and services across the world while building critical skills in supply chain management.

What You'll Do

- Assist in tracking and analyzing supplier performance, purchase orders, and delivery timelines.

- Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations on supply chain metrics.

- Support sourcing activities by gathering quotes, conducting supplier research, and benchmarking costs.

- Work with internal stakeholders to troubleshoot supply issues and identify process improvements.

- Participate in supplier meetings and cross-functional discussions to gain exposure to real-world negotiations and decision-making.

- Document and standardize processes to help build scalable systems.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; comfortable working with spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets).

- Curiosity and eagerness to learn about global supply chain operations in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work on cross-functional projects.

- Organizational skills and attention to detail, with a willingness to dive into both strategic and tactical tasks.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January 2027 to April/May 2027.

The hourly rate for this internship is $37 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

THE COMPANY

Tracing our roots to 1928, Wellington Management Company, LLP (WMC) is one of the world’s largest independent investment management firms. With over $1 trillion in assets under management, we serve as a trusted adviser to institutional clients and mutual fund sponsors in over 60 countries. Our innovative investment solutions are built on the strength of proprietary, independent research and span nearly all segments of the global capital markets, including equity, fixed income, multi-asset, and alternative strategies. As a private partnership whose sole business is investment management, our long-term views and interests are aligned with those of our clients. We are committed to attracting a talented and diverse workforce, and to fostering an open, collaborative culture of inclusivity because we believe multiple perspectives lead to more informed investment and business decisions. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we welcome people with diverse life experiences, fresh ideas, and specialized subject-matter expertise.

THE POSITION

The co-op will join the Reference Data team within Global Operations in a role that offers broad exposure across investment, operational, and client-facing processes. This position is responsible for ensuring the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of reference data that supports the firm’s investment, infrastructure, and client platforms.

The Reference Data team plays a highly critical role in supporting investment activity, operational integrity, and client servicing across the organization by delivering trusted data relied upon throughout the firm. In this role, the analyst will partner with internal stakeholders and external data vendors, perform essential data operations, and help drive continuous improvement in data quality, controls, and scalable processes that support the investment lifecycle. This is a strong opportunity for someone who is intellectually curious, collaborative, and motivated to build deep expertise in a function that is foundational to the firm’s success.

RESPONSIBILITIES

To assist the Reference Data Operations team with daily operational functions including:

- Support investment teams with security setup and maintenance across equities, fixed income and derivatives.

- Coordinate with custodian banks to obtain and update cash rates.

- Liaise with Trading, underwriters, market data vendors, and government sources to obtain required documentation on bond issuances.

- Analyze security documentation, including prospectuses and offering documents, to assess portfolio eligibility.

- Leverage market data vendors and rating agencies, including Bloomberg, Markit, and major ratings providers to analyze and validate data changes

- Provide timely, accurate, and thorough support for routine and complex inquiries.

- Assist in developing controls to strengthen daily operational processes.

- Support special projects as directed by management.

QUALIFICATIONS

A successful candidate will have strong academic credentials and an interest in investment management, financial markets, and data-driven operations. Coursework in finance, economics, business management, data science, mathematics, computer science, or a related field is preferred. Candidates should demonstrate strong analytical skills, attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel is required, and exposure to SQL, Bloomberg, or python is a plus. The ideal candidate will communicate effectively, work collaboratively with global teams, ask thoughtful questions, and take a proactive approach to learning and problem solving. Prior internship, co-op, or project experience in financial services, data analysis, operations, or research is helpful but not required.

Please note: This co-op position entails cross-training to ensure optimal performance across functions. The anticipated start date for accepted candidates is December 2026/January 2027.

Only Northeastern University students are eligible for this program.

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? That’s ok. If you believe that you could excel in this role, we encourage you to apply and welcome a chance to review your background. We are dedicated to building and maintaining a diversified workforce and considering a broad array of candidates with a variety of skill, workplace experiences, and backgrounds.

About Flagship Pioneering

Flagship Pioneering is a biotechnology company that invents and builds platform companies that change the world. We bring together the greatest scientific minds with entrepreneurial company builders and assemble the capital to allow them to take courageous leaps. Those big leaps in human health and sustainability exponentially accelerate scientific progress in areas ranging from cancer detection and treatment to nature-positive agriculture.

What sets Flagship apart is our ability to advance biotechnology by uniting life science innovation, company creation, and capital investment under one roof in a way that is largely without precedent. Our scientific founders, entrepreneurial leaders, and professional capital managers are each aligned around an institutionalized process that enables us to innovate and transform for the benefit of people and planet.

Many of the companies Flagship has founded have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies, and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies.

Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program

Welcome to Flagship Pioneering Co-Op Program for the cohort dreaming big and taking courageous leaps.You'll join fellow peers across our ecosystem of companies and learning firsthand how we build first-in-category companies. You’ll have access to enrichment sessions, a dedicated professional development track, and a mentor that help guide you toward your next step. By the end, you will carry on a meaningful project outcome, a genuine network, and a front-row view of how Flagship pioneer new ventures that change the world.

About the Role

This is a hands-on building role. You will work closely with cross-functional stakeholders to design, prototype, and deploy AI-powered solutions that improve how teams work. Projects range from low-code automations using platforms like Zapier, Vercel, and Workato to full-stack applications built with tools like Claude Code and VS Code, written in Python or JavaScript, and deployed on cloud infrastructure like AWS.

You will take ownership of projects from start to finish: understanding a business process, exploring how to redesign it with AI, building a working solution, and iterating until it holds up in practice.

We’re looking for someone who is curious about not just how to build, but how to build well. That means learning to evaluate which tools and approaches fit a given problem, thinking through a design before jumping into code, and being open to feedback on your approach along the way.

Who This Is For

This role is for builders who are curious, resourceful, and eager to learn. You don’t need to know everything, but you should be excited to figure things out. You’re a strong fit if you:

- Have looked at a manual process and thought, “This wouldn’t exist like this if it were built today”

- Like to prototype quickly and learn by building

- Have hands-on experience building with AI tools, models, or APIs, even in personal or school projects

- Are starting to develop instincts for choosing the right tool for the job, not just using the one you know best

- Ask questions about why something is designed a certain way, not just how to make it work

- Care about whether something actually works reliably, not just in a demo

- Are energized by new technology and lean into learning it

- Can explain what you built and why to someone non-technical

Key Responsibilities

- Build and deploy automations using low-code platforms (e.g., Zapier, Workato) and, where needed, custom code (e.g., Python, JavaScript) to automate business workflows

- Integrate AI models via APIs into automation pipelines

- Help deploy and maintain applications on cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS)

- Learn to evaluate different tools and approaches for new projects, considering tradeoffs like speed, complexity, and long-term maintainability

- Test your own work thoroughly, with a focus on accuracy and edge cases, especially for data-sensitive workflows

- Iterate on proof-of-concept solutions based on real-world performance and feedback from business stakeholders

- Keep clear notes on how your solutions are built so others can understand, maintain, and extend them

- Support AI tool pilots and help create training materials that make it easier for non-technical users to adopt AI-enabled workflows

Basic Requirements

- Current graduate student in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field

- Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, JavaScript)

- Basic understanding of APIs, webhooks, and how web services communicate

- Comfort working with AI tools in a development or productivity context

- Strong problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn new tools quickly

Preferred Requirements

- Experience with low-code or no-code automation platforms (e.g., Zapier, Make, Power Automate, Workato)

- Experience building and deploying applications on cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)

- Familiarity with version control (Git) and development environments like VS Code

What We Offer

- Build alongside founders. You’ll work inside the same hypothesis-driven process Flagship uses to conceive and launch first-in-category companies.

- This can be the start of a longer story. Strong co-ops are considered for future opportunities across Flagship and its portfolio companies, not just for this one role.

- Work alongside people who left the safe path. Your colleagues are scientists, engineers, and operators who chose to build something new rather than join something already established.

- Take on real ownership. You're contributing to ventures that are still being defined. Your work can shape real decisions, not just support them.

- Be paid like the contributor you are. Compensation reflects the real work you take on.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Commercial Marketplace Team

The Commercial Marketplace team runs the operating system that connects site-level conditions to commercial action. We track marketplace health across each site, cohort, and metro, balancing demand, selection, customer experience, capacity, utilization, and profitability. By partnering with Product, Operations, Marketing, Finance, and Sales, we identify the right levers - such as prioritization, promotions, pricing, and demand shaping - and help turn them into scalable programs. Our work helps Zipline grow healthy marketplaces while protecting service quality and making the best use of scarce operational and commercial resources. What makes the team special is its combination of quantitative analysis, marketplace judgment, and hands-on execution.

The Role

As a Commercial Marketplace Strategy & Operations Intern, you will help answer questions like what is happening at a site, which sites are best suited for a given growth program, and where capacity or customer experience constraints may limit growth. You’ll use data to prepare readouts, surface opportunities, test hypotheses, and support decisions across Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Utilization. You will learn how marketplace levers such as selection, partner prioritization, pricing, promotions, and demand shaping work together in a real delivery network. Your analyses will inform decisions that improve marketplace health, help scale what works, and expand reliable access to goods.

What You'll Do

- Evaluate and build the playbook for marketplace levers such as pricing, promotions, partner prioritization, pricing, promotions, budget allocation, demand shaping, and customer-experience protection.

- Analyze site and cohort performance to identify where to prioritize sales resources, marketing actions, product rollouts, operational playbooks, or other growth programs.

- Build and maintain recurring reports and dashboards, partnering with Analytics as needed to improve visibility into site, cohort, and metro performance.

- Support daily and weekly site-level performance readouts across marketplace health, growth, efficiency, utilization, fulfillment, customer outcomes, and profitability.

- Monitor aircraft availability, fulfillment throughput, throttling, and operational constraints; surface risks that could affect growth plans or customer experience.

- Partner with Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Utilization to turn insights into action, measure results, and scale what works.

What You'll Bring

- Currently enrolled in a master’s degree program.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using spreadsheets or similar tools to organize, analyze, and communicate data.

- Ability to investigate performance at different levels of detail - from a single site to a cohort or metro - and turn findings into a clear recommendation.

- Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting findings to cross-functional partners.

- A collaborative, self-directed working style and curiosity about marketplaces, logistics, and how technology can improve access to goods.

- Able to work full-time onsite in South San Francisco for the duration of the Spring 2027 internship.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

- Python experience

- JavaScript experience

The NVIDIA Architecture Research Group is seeking an intern to help define the future of GPU and data-center computing. Our research spans GPU microarchitecture, memory systems and memory models, large-scale data-center hardware, emerging accelerators, and the architecture implications of new workloads in AI, scientific computing, robotics, and other rapidly evolving domains. Are you excited about exploring foundational research questions, developing new architectural ideas, and helping translate those ideas into future NVIDIA systems?

In this position, you will apply your knowledge of computer architecture, parallel computing, compilers, runtime systems, and workloads to explore new hardware and hardware–software co-design opportunities. You will work with researchers and product architects to formulate research questions, develop and evaluate architecture concepts, and build the models, simulators, prototypes, and experimental infrastructure needed to test them. Projects may range from mechanisms within a GPU to memory consistency and programmability, rack- and data-center-scale architectures, and specialized hardware for emerging applications.

You should have a strong foundation in computer architecture and parallel systems, an ability to work across hardware and software boundaries, and experience with some combination of architecture modeling, simulation, workload analysis, compilers, runtime systems, or CPU/GPU programming. You should also be comfortable building robust research prototypes and communicating the insights produced by your work. NVIDIA pioneered programmable GPUs and CUDA and continues to shape the future of accelerated computing. This position offers an opportunity to conduct ambitious research and have a direct impact on future products.

What you’ll be doing:

- Investigate new architecture concepts for future GPUs, memory systems, accelerators, and data-center-scale computing platforms.

- Study emerging workloads and identify the architectural bottlenecks and opportunities they create.

- Explore hardware–software co-design across architecture, compilers, runtime systems, programming models, and applications.

- Develop models, simulators, prototypes, and experimental tools to evaluate new architecture ideas.

- Research new approaches to memory hierarchy, coherence, consistency, data movement, and system-level programmability.

- Collaborate with NVIDIA researchers, GPU architects, software teams, and product groups to develop and evaluate promising concepts.

- Clearly communicate research findings through presentations, technical reports, and potentially research publications.

- Help transfer successful research ideas, methodologies, and tools into NVIDIA product teams.

What we need to see:

- Pursuing PhD Degree in relevant discipline(s) (CS, CE, EE, Physics, Math).

- Relevant industrial and University experience. Relevant industries include hardware, software, and algorithm development in PC or workstation graphics, digital video or image processing, video game or console, cell phones or consumer electronics, rendering software, and computing.

- Strong programming ability in C/C++, and scripting languages.

- Experience as a CUDA programmer.

- Background with building computer system simulators.

- Experience building efficient low-level software tools such as runtime systems, binary translators, or compilers.

- Strong background in computer architecture and parallel computer architectures.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

- Prior research experience and/or research publications at ISCA/MICRO/ASPLOS/HPCA/MLSYS

- Versatile in using generative AI coding tools

- Versatile in using GPU profiling tools and running DL models on GPUs

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. Are you creative and independently driven? Do you love a challenge? Come join our Architecture Research Group and help us invent the future of Computing.

Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The hourly rate for our interns is 38 USD - 94 USD.

You will also be eligible for Intern benefits. ​

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 16, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying.

At Klaviyo, our Engineering teams build scalable, high-performance systems that power both our product and the infrastructure behind it. As a Software Engineering Co-op, you'll be part of a fast-paced, collaborative team whose work reaches thousands of customers worldwide. You won't just be writing code. You'll be solving hard problems, shaping how users experience our product, and learning from engineers who've been doing this for a while.

This co-op is your shot to put your software development skills to work in production. You'll be embedded on one of our engineering teams (see overviews below), take on projects that matter to our customers, and build a technical foundation as you make connections across the business.

Our co-ops come from all kinds of coding backgrounds, but they all share one thing: they're excited to build, own, and scale features end-to-end, from scratch. You'll work alongside experienced engineers, take on hard technical problems, and ship code that supports Klaviyo's mission. We're an AI-first company, so you'll be expected to use AI tools to support your work, learn faster, and do your best work here.

How you'll make an impact

- Own features that our 180K+ paying customers rely on daily to reach their consumers and grow their business.

- Take responsibility for the mission, technical direction, and operation of projects with immediate impact.

- Own the full lifecycle of your code: writing it, testing it, shipping it, and making it better over time. Ownership is expected here, not just encouraged.

- Build and ship features that meet a high bar and grow your technical skills while you do it.

- Get hands-on debugging real issues, both locally and in production.

- Contribute to documentation and support your team during incidents (real-world problems teach you things a tutorial never will).

- Work closely with your teammates: ask questions, share ideas, and get better by taking feedback seriously.

- Learn to use the right tool for the job, lean into AI, and keep looking for ways to make things better.

- Put AI at the center of how you work to move faster. Build smarter systems and better workflows from the ground up.

Who you are

- At least one previous software engineering internship or co-op, with hands-on software development experience

- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Math/Statistics, or a related field

- Graduating in December 2027 or May/June 2028

- Experience with some of these technologies and languages:

- Python, Django, Typescript, React, Go

- MySQL, Cassandra, Clickhouse, Kafka, Redis

- Amazon Web Services (EC2, RDS, Aurora, etc.), Terraform

- You enjoy working across new technologies and you’re excited to work across the stack from back-end to front-end work

- You love digging into performance and scalability issues to find breakthrough solutions: a slow-loading UI, too many clicks in a workflow, a database query timing out, a queue that won't drain. You believe every problem can be solved, and you'd rather run toward it than around it.

- You enjoy shipping code early and often, working closely with products to build better software based on feedback from thousands of end users.

- You embrace Klaviyo's "always learning" culture. We learn faster together, which is part of why this program happens in person.

- You've already experimented with AI in work or personal projects, and you're excited to find ways to make your work smarter and more efficient.

Co-op logistics

- Our Spring Co-op Program is a paid experience [January 4–June 25] at our Boston, MA headquarters. Co-ops are in office 5 days a week.

- Offers will be team agnostic. Co-ops are placed on a team approximately 30 days from the start of the program. Team placement can be on a full-stack, back-end, or front-end team within any of the pillars.

- Before joining individual teams, all co-ops go through Klaviyo Base Camp, our onboarding experience built to get you up to speed on Klaviyo, our product, and the day-to-day of engineering here.

- Our Boston office is genuinely fun. Lunch is on us 5 days a week, along with free snacks and drinks, ping pong, Nintendo Switch, a golf simulator, and a speakeasy to unwind in.

- Throughout the program, co-ops get together for social events beyond team and project work: a Red Sox game, trips to Versus and Activate, ice cream socials, and Ask Me Anything sessions with Klaviyo's senior leadership.

- Apply before October 7 if you can. We interview and hire on a rolling basis.

Former co-op projects

- Redesigned and refactored the email editor component architecture for performance and scalability, including reusable shared components and testing coverage improvements.

- Developed and deployed a new invite management microservice handling multiple roles, statuses, and integrations with audit logs.

- Built a real-time data ingestion and aggregation pipeline using kinesis and redshift, with monitoring and validation.

- Designed and implemented an automated rollback system that detects new unhandled sentry errors and notifies deployers via Slack.

- Own the WhatsApp double opt-in (DOI) feature end-to-end, integrating backend validation, frontend UI, and monitoring dashboards.

- Integrated AI-assisted tools into build validation pipelines, measuring productivity impact and creating internal best practices guide.

Engineering at Klaviyo

Our engineering teams are organized into pillars to keep the work focused.

- Data Infrastructure: Empower our internal teams and customers to get the best out of our data and agent platforms. underlying capabilities: Agent Platform, CDP revenue, Data Lake usage, Active API endpoints, Accounts with healthy API usage

- MCMI: Own the growth, revenue, and reliability of our mobile channels and all messaging infrastructure.

- Core Infrastructure: Empower our internal engineering, sales, and service teams to be as effective as possible by improving productivity of the eng, product, and design teams.

- Growth Marketing Platform: Give marketers the tools they need to engage with their customers, be successful, and know where they stand.

- AI & Analytics: Applies AI, data, and analytics to automate work, surface insights, and help customers make smarter decisions that maximize Klaviyo Attributed Value (KAV).

- Autonomous Service: Builds AI-powered customer service experiences that help resolve issues, support transactions, and connect customers with human assistance when needed.

- Product Security: Engineer the proactive defenses, detection systems, and response tooling that safeguard Klaviyo's customers and their data.

If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't check every box, apply anyway. Some of the strongest Klaviyos didn't start with a perfect resume match.

The Recommendation Foundation team within TikTok’s Data – Global E-commerce organization is dedicated to building shared Recommendation Foundation Models across scenarios. Packaging Engineer Intern

Location: San Jose, California, United States
Employment type: Internship
Organization: Packaging / Engineering Operations

About Astera Labs

Astera Labs is a semiconductor company developing intelligent connectivity solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. Our products depend on high-performance interconnects and advanced semiconductor packaging to move data reliably across compute, memory, and storage systems.

Role overview

As a Semiconductor Packaging Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will help enhance key areas of the package development cycle, including package design, modeling, automation flows, and documentation.

You will work cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone interested in the interaction between electrical performance, power delivery, thermal behavior, mechanical constraints, and manufacturability. You will contribute to package-design and modeling work, document your results, and help the team make well-supported engineering decisions.

Responsibilities

- Support package design, modeling, automation, and documentation for Astera Labs’ connectivity products.

- Collaborate cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle.

- Support package definition by organizing inputs such as die files, pin-out details, signal- and power-integrity requirements, thermal requirements, board and footprint constraints, supplier design rules, cost considerations, and reliability needs.

- Help maintain package Plan of Record (POR) information, including package structure, substrate stackup and materials, package SI/PI requirements, thermal requirements, development schedule, and open risks.

- Generate or review package netlists from die files and package footprints, and support package layout work with internal or external design partners.

- Import and prepare package layout data for analysis; verify nets, stackups, materials, vias, bumps, and BGA or solder-ball geometries against available design and manufacturing information.

- Support package-level signal-integrity and power-integrity analysis using tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS 3D Layout, SIwave, and Keysight ADS as appropriate to the project.

- Set up ports and target nets, extract S-parameters, analyze insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk, impedance, and related channel behavior, and compare results with design requirements.

- Support power-integrity studies such as DCIR, PDN impedance, and transient or frequency-domain analysis; help interpret voltage drop, current density, resonance, and impedance results.

- Assist with thermal and mechanical analyses by organizing material and structural inputs, reviewing results, and helping identify risks related to temperature, stress, warpage, or reliability.

- Review package layouts against substrate and OSAT design rules and support design-for-manufacturing activities such as density checks, degassing considerations, and design-rule checks.

- Contribute to package tape-out and NPI readiness reviews by checking documentation and tracking open actions.

- Help prepare and maintain package documentation, including bills of materials, netlists, package outline or lid information, substrate stackup drawings, and electrical, thermal, or mechanical models when applicable.

- Support communication with substrate suppliers and OSAT partners by organizing questions, requirements, feedback, and manufacturing-readiness information.

- Document assumptions, simulation setups, results, issues, and recommendations in a clear and reusable format; present project learnings at the end of the internship.

Basic qualifications

- Working towards an M.S. or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

- Cumulative GPA of 3.3/4.0 or higher.

- Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.

- Ability to work with minimal supervision and deliver solutions in a fast-paced environment.

- Strong time-management skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.

Required experience

- Coursework in RF/microwave, communication systems and signal analysis, semiconductor manufacturing, or circuit design.

- Understanding of or coursework in signal and power integrity is a plus.

- Understanding of or coursework in semiconductor packaging is a plus.

- Scripting or software-development experience in Python, Visual Basic, or equivalent programming languages.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to detail when working with geometry, models, data, and documentation.

- Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across disciplines, and follow through on defined tasks.

Preferred experience

- Experience with physical-design or layout tools such as AutoCAD, Cadence Allegro, Cadence APD/SiP, or comparable tools.

- Experience using 3D electromagnetic-simulation tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS, HFSS 3D Layout, or SIwave.

- Knowledge of semiconductor multilayer flip-chip packages, including FCBGA or FCCSP.

- Experience with package substrate stackups, copper pillars, solder bumps, BGA balls, package-to-board transitions, or high-density interconnects.

- Familiarity with S-parameter extraction and validation, including ports, Touchstone models, passivity, causality, de-embedding, or mixed-mode analysis.

- Exposure to power-integrity concepts such as IR drop, DCIR, PDN impedance, decoupling, or current-density analysis.

- Experience with thermal modeling, mechanical analysis, coefficient-of-thermal-expansion effects, warpage, reliability, or package materials.

- Familiarity with design-for-manufacturing, supplier design rules, package assembly, reflow, underfill, or OSAT workflows.

- Experience using Python, MATLAB, Visual Basic, spreadsheets, or similar tools to automate analysis, process engineering data, or communicate results.

- Prior semiconductor, package-design, hardware, supplier, or manufacturing experience through coursework, research, projects, or an internship.

What success looks like

- You learn the packaging development flow and the team’s analysis tools, then take ownership of a defined technical task with appropriate guidance.

- You produce accurate, traceable analysis or documentation; communicate assumptions and risks early; and follow open actions through to closure.

- By the end of the internship, you have contributed useful results to a package-design, SI/PI, thermal/mechanical, DFM, tape-out, or manufacturing-readiness workstream and can clearly explain your approach, findings, and impact.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Equal opportunity

Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply.

Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

The Advanced Computing Solutions Group in the NLR Computational Science Center has an opening for a full-time Postdoctoral Researcher – Computational Sciences, with an emphasis on mathematical optimization and its application to the design and control of energy systems. We are looking for a dynamic researcher with a strong technical background to help us transform our energy future through advanced automation, control and decision making.

The successful candidate will have extensive experience with mathematical optimization formulations and algorithms and their application to physical systems. Additionally, the candidate will be familiar with parallel algorithmic approaches for large-scale linear, nonlinear, integer, and stochastic optimization problems. We anticipate that the research will involve integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, such as reinforcement learning (RL), with classical mathematical optimization approaches and implementations. We seek candidates capable of pursuing research directions that combine these algorithmic components, using implementations that are suitable for effective utilization of the modern parallel computing architectures that are available at NRL. Candidates with creative problem-solving skills, interest in cross-disciplinary collaboration, and a passion for the mission and goals of both NLR and CMEI are of particular interest.

Responsibilities:

- Collaborate with domain experts to identify where mathematical optimization constitutes a viable approach and maintain awareness of optimization-related research both at NLR and in the literature more generally.
- Adopt existing – or develop new – mathematical, computing, and simulation frameworks required to implement and evaluate the performance of optimization algorithms and solutions.
- Creatively identify new opportunities to leverage AI/RL to augment or enhance classical optimization algorithms and/or formulations.

- Author publications and contribute to proposals to sustain research directions.

.

Basic Qualifications

Must be a recent PhD graduate within the last three years.

* Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date.

Additional Required Qualifications

- Experience formulating optimization problems in an algebraic modeling language, e.g., Pyomo, JuMP, PuLP, GAMS.
- Experience with mathematical optimization solvers, e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi, Xpress, Cbc, Ipopt, and their capabilities.
- Good understanding of optimization fundamentals, both computational and mathematical.

Preferred Qualifications

- Familiarity with distributed computing frameworks such as MPI and OpenMP
- Experience with Pyomo and/or JuMP
- Experience programming in Python and/or Julia
- Experience with scalable machine learning frameworks, e.g, PyTorch
- Experience working with diverse, inclusive, and cross-disciplinary research teams

.

Meta Reality Labs Research is a team of researchers and engineers pushing the frontier of AI and robotics. Our team is building the next generation of world action models (WAMs) and vision-language-action models (VLAs) for robotic manipulation. We are seeking a Research Scientist Intern to develop scalable methods for mid-training world action models on large-scale egocentric video and robot data.

Interns in this role will conduct fundamental and applied research to advance foundation models for robotics, with a focus on mid-training. You will collaborate with research scientists and engineers to develop new algorithms, build and evaluate model capabilities, and contribute to the next generation of embodied AI.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities

Develop scalable mid-training methods for WAMs using large-scale egocentric video and heterogeneous robot data. Investigate representation and objective design for learning from human egocentric video. Address challenges in training on web-scale, weakly-labeled data, including embodiment and viewpoint gaps, data curation and filtering, and domain mixture weighting. Build efficient training and data pipelines, and study how downstream policy performance scales with dataset size, model capacity, and compute. Design experiments and benchmarks to measure what mid-training contributes, isolating its effect on downstream post-training and generalization across tasks and embodiments. Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to evaluate mid-trained models in simulation and on real robots. Communicate research findings and publish results at leading machine learning, computer vision, and robotics venues.

Qualifications

Currently has or is in the process of obtaining a Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, or a related STEM field Research experience in training of video models or robotics foundation models Experience implementing and training deep learning models using Python and PyTorch or a comparable framework Experience designing controlled experiments, analyzing results, and debugging machine learning algorithms Interpersonal experience: cross-group and cross-culture collaboration Must obtain work authorization in country of employment at the time of hire and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment Intent to return to degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op Experience training VLAs, WAMs, or other foundation models for embodied decision-making Experience with diffusion or flow-based policies, action-sequence prediction, or action-conditioned world models Hands-on experience with distributed training across multiple GPUs or nodes, including improving training throughput, memory efficiency, and stability Experience evaluating learned policies on physical robots or robotics simulation benchmarks Proven track record of achieving significant results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, and/or accepted papers in top conferences or journals such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ACL, etc

About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

As a Power Systems Engineering Intern on Base’s Risk & Trading team, you’ll help model how our network of distributed residential batteries interacts with the grid, at both the distribution and transmission levels. During your internship you’ll be tasked with important problems for the business and expected to deliver just like any other full-time member of the team. You’ll work alongside Base’s power systems engineers on power flow studies, grid models, and the analysis behind where our batteries are deployed and how they’re dispatched.

This is hands-on engineering work with real stakeholders. The studies and tools you build will be used by Base’s operations and business development teams and can shape how we work with utilities and grid operators. You’ll own a scoped project end to end, from defining the study and building the model to presenting what you found.

What You’ll Do

- Help design and run power flow studies (e.g., steady-state and contingency analyses) for Base battery aggregation use cases.

- Build and validate distribution and transmission system models, using standard test topologies such as the IEEE test feeders.

- Write Python to automate studies so they can be solved programmatically and run on a recurring basis.

- Analyze and visualize study results and grid data, and turn them into clear recommendations, such as where on a feeder Base’s systems create the most value.

- Compile and present your results to power systems engineers and the broader Risk & Trading team.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related technical field.

- Coursework, research, or project experience in power systems: power flow, per-unit systems, and three-phase analysis.

- Proficiency in Python for data analysis and visualization (e.g., pandas, NumPy, matplotlib).

- A strong foundation in linear algebra and numerical methods (e.g., Newton-Raphson).

- A strong ownership mindset and the ability to clearly explain your assumptions, methods, and results.

- Nice to have: exposure to power flow tools such as OpenDSS, GridLAB-D, CYME, PSS/E, PowerWorld, PyPSA, or pandapower, or to optimal power flow and electricity markets (e.g., ERCOT).

About the Team

Base’s Risk & Trading team is tasked with ensuring the grid-support performance and profitability of Base’s distributed battery fleet. This encompasses device communications with balancing authorities, telemetry analysis, algorithms for fleet aggregation and economic dispatch, through to financial portfolio management in wholesale energy markets. Our power systems engineers are the team’s experts on how the fleet interacts with the grid, from distribution feeders to the bulk transmission system. Our team is made up of physicists, economists, computer scientists, and engineers; the best candidates will bring the day-over-day intensity of an operator with the foresight to drive the long term development of simpler, more performant automated control. Success looks like building the airplane as it falls out of the sky.

Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.

Our Values

- First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

- Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

- Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

- Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

- Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

- Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

- Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

Do the best work of your life at Base.

The Biologics Formulation Research Internship focuses on the analytical characterization and formulation of biologic drug candidates to support the development of stable pharmaceutical products for manufacturing in microgravity. Interns will apply a variety of biophysical and analytical techniques to evaluate protein structure, stability, binding interactions, and performance through formulation and freeze-drying processes. The role combines hands-on laboratory experimentation, scientific data analysis, and close collaboration with formulation scientists to advance next-generation biologic therapeutics.

Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company's success. You will be working on a collaborative team in a startup environment while being able to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the world. We're dedicated to providing an experience that will let your decisions and contributions help drive Varda's success.

Responsibilities

- Perform biophysical characterization of protein candidates using orthogonal analytical techniques to assess structure, stability, and interaction behavior

- Design and execute binding and selection studies between disordered protein stabilizers and microcrystalline pharmaceutical substrates

- Evaluate stabilizer performance through lyophilization and reconstitution cycles, assessing protein integrity before and after freeze-drying stress

- Conduct purity and charge variant analysis via SDS-PAGE and capillary isoelectric focusing (cIEF)

- Prepare reagents, buffers, and sample sets in advance to ensure experiments run on schedule

- Maintain accurate, well-documented records in laboratory notebooks and electronic systems

- Collaborate with formulation scientists to anticipate laboratory needs and contribute to team meetings and progress updates

Key Techniques & Methods

Interns will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard biophysical and analytical tools, including:

- Nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF)

- Analytical size exclusion chromatography (SEC)

- Dynamic light scattering (DLS)

- Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy

- UV spectroscopy

- Fluorescence spectroscopy

- SDS-PAGE and capillary isoelectric focusing (cIEF)

- Selection and binding studies

- General familiarity with lyophilization and tangential flow filtration (TFF) as they relate to sample preparation and handling

What You'll Learn

- How to characterize protein and peptide structure, stability, and molecular interactions using multiple orthogonal biophysical techniques

- How to design and interpret binding and interaction studies between disordered proteins/peptides and crystalline substrates

- How biophysical characterization connects to formulation strategy and long-term storage stability for biologic drugs

- Best practices in analytical method execution, data interpretation, and scientific documentation in a biotech R&D environment

- Strong attention to detail and ability to follow experimental protocols precisely

- Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities

- Effective written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Skills & Experience

- Familiarity with one or more of the listed biophysical characterization techniques (DLS, nanoDSF, SEC, CD, or capillary electrophoresis)

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

NEW GRADUATE ENGINEER, SOFTWARE (STARSHIP)

Our SpaceX team is working on the toughest and most audacious projects on our planet: making humanity multiplanetary. SpaceX's Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket (collectively referred to as Starship) represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Starship will be the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, with the ability to carry in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth orbit.

As a Software Engineer on the Starship Software team, you will design, develop, and test software that is used to both control and simulate SpaceX flight systems. You will engage with other SpaceX software and hardware engineers to implement and debug software at all layers of our stack – application, operating system, networking, firmware, simulation – to achieve the mission. Our development timelines are quick and you will need to rigorously explore solutions for previously unsolved or unknown problems. Every day, we push the limits of what is possible through innovation, determination, and teamwork to drive the mission to success.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Expect a dynamic role doing what you’re best at. Our team is building high-performance flight hardware. Whatever your skill set, you’ll be aligned to the part of the program you’re most effectively able to contribute to.

- Develop highly reliable autonomous software systems and the simulations required to validate them.

- Own all aspects of software development, including design, testing, and integration to the mission.

- Work with counterpart engineering teams to develop and maintain launch and vehicle software.

- Get a front row seat to witness an impossible idea manifest in real life. The next few years will be incredibly dynamic as we transition from the challenge of building hardware to actually flying reusable rockets to orbit and deploying complex satellites to orbit.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, computer engineering, electrical engineering or other engineering discipline.

- Graduating with a bachelor's degree, master's degree, or PhD in 2027.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Proven skills and knowledge of C++, Rust, or other systems programming language.

- Experience building or working with real-time embedded systems or distributed computing systems.

- Strong focus and interest in designing, architecting, and implementing excellent, bug-free software.

- Strong critical thinking and first-principles problem-solving skills.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Able to work effectively in a dynamic environment while assuming high levels of responsibility and demonstrating accountability for software outcomes.

- Experience working at a nimble engineering organization or in a highly technical position that required a scrappy, entrepreneurial manner to accomplish tasks with tight time or budget constraints.

- Excelled in ultra-competitive environments. You’ve nailed a podium finish in engineering, math, or science competitions, achieved scores in the top percentile of scholastic or standardized tests, or demonstrated other incredible feats of intellectual achievement.

- Succeeded in multiple endeavors at once. Maybe you worked through college, were a student athlete, or demonstrated strong work or academic performance in multiple fields.

- Demonstrated rapid growth. You’ve held successive positions of increasing responsibility within an organization, were able to get yourself up to speed at a heroic pace, and accomplished something meaningfully difficult early in your career.

- Success in academics at a rigorous and highly regarded university: minimum GPA 3.5/4.0 or higher, standardized test scores minimum 95th percentile, merit-based scholarship recipient.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

- Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Software Engineer/Level I: $125,000.00 - $150,000.00/per year
Software Engineer/Level II: $145,000.00 - $175,000.00/per year

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock, stock options, or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Exempt employees are eligible for 5 days of sick leave per year.

The Northrop Grumman Military Internship Program (NG-MIP) is an approved SkillBridge Program under Dept. of Defense Instruction 1322.29 . NG-MIP is an opportunity for transitioning service members to gain valuable civilian work experience through an individual internship during their last 6 months of service, for up to 180 days. The Northrop Grumman Military Internship Program is open to all ranks and experience levels. SkillBridge participants are not eligible for compensation from Northrop Grumman, as they continue to receive military compensation and benefits as active-duty service members.

Northrop Grumman Corporation (NGC) has developed the Northrop Grumman – Military Internship Program (SKillbridge) utilizing the DoDI guidance for Skillbridge. During this program the service member will be on-site at his or her host company performing an individual internship in an entry to mid-level career type role. The service member will be on the job training supporting a work schedule equivalent to 40hrs per week. Outlined below are the Goals, Objectives, and Outcomes for the program.

Goals – Provide transitioning service members fellowship-style job skills training during the last portion(s) of their military commitment. This program is specifically designed to offer internships that result in the potential to transition to a full-time opportunity as the conclusion of the training. Interns will serve as a pipeline for high-speed, motivated military candidates into NGC.

This program provides a comprehensive internship experience including professional development, networking with leadership, and training specifically focused on NG leadership principles, company history, customer/stakeholder engagement, product and service overview, and core job responsibilities.

Outcome – Offer transitioning service member a rewarding opportunity to join the Northrop Grumman team.

Agios is a full stack research organization within Reality Labs Research, spanning materials and manufacturing, sensors and actuators, simulation, and learned control. Our mission is to build systems that enhance human capabilities through intelligent machine collaboration. Today that work centers on what we call the last bottleneck: AI has compressed the digital side of research and development, while the physical side still moves at human speed. Dexterous Manipulation is the pillar attacking that problem directly, pairing a custom dexterous robotic hand with in-house wearable sensing, high accuracy simulation, and glove-driven teleoperation.

As a Research Scientist Intern, you will work at the intersection of robot learning, dexterous control, and human-to-robot transfer, with mentors who span hardware, simulation, controls, and policy learning. Your focus will be learned models that turn human demonstration data into executable robot behavior, covering retargeting, manipulation policies, and teleoperation.
Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities

Drive an independent research thread on learned control and motion transfer for dexterous hands, from problem formulation through real robot or high fidelity simulation evaluation. Build training pipelines for modern policy classes, including flow matching and diffusion policies, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, large behavior models, and VLAs. Develop representations that fuse multimodal human and robot data, including video, hand pose, tactile and contact force, and IMU, into a shared action space. Construct data collection pipelines and benchmarks for dexterous manipulation, including held-out and out-of-distribution protocols that test generalization across objects, motions, and embodiments. Collaborate across an interdisciplinary team of hardware, simulation, controls, and policy researchers, and communicate research plans, progress, and results.

dexterous manipulation and control, with judgment about which open problems are worth advancing Experience with Python and PyTorch or JAX, plus familiarity with ROS or comparable robotics middleware demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, as well as first-authored publications at leading workshops or conferences such as Robotics (RSS, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, T-RO, IJRR), Machine Learning (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, JMLR), and Computer Vision (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, TPAMI), or similar Experience training modern control policies, including flow matching, diffusion, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and large behavior models Familiarity with modeling and analysis used in robotics including kinematics, dynamics, trajectory optimization, motion planning, perception, task In this role, you will evolve the Keysight Network Visibility (NVS) product line to support Service Provider features and newer technologies (e.g. 5G, 6G core network 3GPP standards). The NVS products allow our customers to tap, aggregate, filter, sample, and perform many other functions on network traffic for monitoring and analysis.

Keysight’s network packet broker provides multiple applications:

- MobileStack – monitoring of customer traffic from a mobile user/session perspective (e.g. GTP, SIP/RTP)
- AppStack – monitoring of customer traffic from an application perspective (i.e. L4-L7)
- SecureStack – providing secure encryption/decryption for TLS1.3 (Active SSL)
- TradeVision – stock trading monitoring and analysis tool
- PacketStack – standard packet broker features such as aggregation, deduplication, masking, etc.
- NetStack – port tagging and VLAN stripping
- KVO – Keysight Vision Orchestrator – manages all the products and applications

The focus of this job will be on mobility related functionality for the Service Providers, such as control plane/user plane correlation, meta data and orchestration. This includes virtualization of products and machine learning applications.

Our MobileStack application tracks mobile users and sessions, sending the associated control and user plane data to specific network monitoring tools (i.e. probes) for analysis. In addition, the application load balances across probes and provides sampling, filtering, and VIP allow listing functionalities. This allows our customers to manage their probe bandwidth by looking at a subset of the overall network traffic, in addition to being able to troubleshoot specific quality of service issues. As network traffic continues to increase each year, our customers need solutions to monitor their network traffic more efficiently and cost effectively.

Why co-ops are core to how we build our team 🎓

At Rundoo, hiring co-op students who come back full-time after graduation is core to how we build our team. Students who pair rigorous academics with hands-on co-op experience become builders who have immediate impact and grow quickly. That holds just as true for Marketing Engineering as it does for core Engineering.

We're looking for our first Marketing Engineering intern to help prove out this pipeline. If it's a fit, we're committed to hiring more each term and building the function around you.

Term 📅

Winter 2027: January 4 – April 23.

What You'll Achieve with Us: Ship Marketing Agents and Automations 💼

This isn't about busywork or one-off decks. You'll build the internal tools, agents and automations that power how Rundoo markets itself, and you'll see your work go live every day! This role focuses on internal marketing tooling, not customer-facing product work.

- Agent & Workflow Development: Help build and maintain automations and agents that generate marketing content (ads, emails, social posts) at scale.

- Data Pipelines & Integrations: Connect the tools in our marketing stack (ads, email, direct mail and more) so data moves between systems accurately and efficiently.

- Campaign Instrumentation: Help instrument and monitor live campaigns so every program, and every dollar of ad spend, can be traced back to pipeline and ARR impact.

- Attribution & Reporting: Help map marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced leads through the funnel: MQL → SQL → Opp → Closed Won.

- Content Systems: Prototype reusable templates and agents for recurring content types (magazine ads, digital postcards, newsletter banners, social posts, flyers) that support our vertical GTM motions.

- Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with our Head of Marketing, CEO and vertical PMs to keep automations grounded in real campaign needs.

Hard requirements ☑️

- You're comfortable writing code and can show us a GitHub with example work.

- You're genuinely excited about applying AI and agents to marketing problems, not just interested in marketing as a discipline.

- You're a self-directed builder who can turn a rough campaign idea into a working automation.

- You give in-the-moment feedback to your teammates and enjoy receiving the same.

Nice to have ⭐

- Experience building data pipelines or integrations that connect tools and move data between systems.

- Experience building workflows with an LLM in the mix, like RAG or scripts that call the Claude or OpenAI APIs.

- Experience deploying simple apps or services (Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, Coder.dev or similar).

- Familiarity with marketing and growth concepts (MQLs, attribution, funnel metrics, ad automation).

- Comfort working with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) to build end-to-end workflows.

Interview Process 🎤

- Application: must include a GitHub account with example work.

- Intro Call (20 min, remote): Meet Amanda to learn more about each other and talk through your interest in marketing + AI automation.

Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. - Product development processes from concept to customer-facing demonstrations.

- Develop Python-based data processing and visualization workflows.

Contribute to demonstrations that support customer engagement, conferences, webinars, and future product releases.

- Computer Science
- Software Engineering
- Computer Engineering
- Related technical field

- Experience with Python programming.
- Experience with object-oriented software development.
- Familiarity with data structures and software design principles.
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

- Experience with JavaScript or TypeScript.
- Experience developing web applications.

Datadog AI Research (DAIR) is partnering with Carnegie Mellon University to support a small number of PhD students working on open research problems grounded by ongoing efforts at Datadog/DAIR.

- Leadership opportunities on specific internship program activities and/or group projects

Join the power movement as a Scientific Software Engineering Intern

We are looking for a talented Scientific Software Engineering Intern to join our team! CFS interns are highly valued within the organization and placed into meaningful and challenging roles.

Program Details:

- 13-18 week internship

- 40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school

- Opportunities on site in Devens, MA. If an intern is going to be on site, you will be responsible for your own transportation and housing

- Interns must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer

What you'll do:

- Port high-performance electromagnetics kernels to the GPU. You’ll start with the Biot-Savart magnetic-field calculation in cfsem, CFS’s open-source Rust library, and extend it to include cross-platform GPU kernel variants with Python bindings

- Hold your code to a scientific-correctness bar. You’ll check the GPU kernels against cfsem’s existing unit tests and CPU versions, and determine if your methods are accurate enough for engineers who rely on the results to design superconducting magnets

- Measure and report GPU performance. You’ll benchmark speed and accuracy against the optimized multithreaded Rust CPU kernels, and present a clear recommendation on where GPU acceleration pays off and where it doesn’t

- Ship public open-source work. You’ll put the new kernels behind cfsem’s existing Python interface so they reach CFS engineers working on SPARC and future fusion magnets, and you’ll leave with merged contributions to a public Rust/Python project

- Pursuing an engineering degree with focus in the field of Computer Science

- Contributed to a multi-person software project

- Rust programming language

- Software performance engineering (class, project or internship experience)

- Willingness to travel or work required nights/weekends/on-call occasionally
