- Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. At Graviton, every strategy, model and edge begins not with instinct, but with someone asking a better question than everyone else.

As a Quantitative Research Intern, you'll spend 10-12 weeks working on research that directly shapes how we understand markets and build trading strategies. You'll collaborate with researchers and technologists to investigate market behaviour, test hypotheses, build predictive models and solve problems where the answers aren't obvious.

This isn't an internship where you observe from the sidelines. Outstanding work has the potential to shape production strategies and generate real, measurable returns.

Ideal candidates are quantitatively sharp, practically minded problem solvers, programmers, mathematicians and scientists who are excited to solve the hardest problems in our field, across our offices in the US, Singapore, Amsterdam and London.

What You'll Work On

You'll work on real research problems, not simulated exercises, discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events, designing statistical models, and applying machine learning to open research problems. Your work would include:

- Discovering predictive patterns from billions of market events

- Designing statistical models that identify trading opportunities

- Applying probability, optimization and machine learning to open research problems

- Building AI-powered research agents that accelerate experimentation

- Developing infrastructure for rapid, large-scale research

- Designing experiments and backtests to evaluate hypotheses

- Translating research into production-ready trading signals

- Exploring new ML, AI and quant finance techniques to find the next source of alpha

What You'll Learn

Beyond the technical exposure, you'll learn how experienced researchers approach hard problems: breaking them down, questioning assumptions, and deciding based on evidence rather than intuition. You'll be paired with a mentor, reporting manager and buddy, with regular code reviews and feedback throughout the internship.

What Success Looks Like

Successful interns leave having delivered a complete research project from hypothesis to evaluation, built statistically rigorous models, and demonstrated curiosity, ownership and the ability to solve open-ended problems.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional students who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems.

- Full-time undergraduate, Master's or PhD student in a quantitative discipline (math, physics, computer science, statistics, or a related field), graduating 2028

- Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

- Grounded in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

- Comfortable working with large, complex datasets, with strong analytical thinking

- A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

- Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Our Culture

More than specific technologies, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to question assumptions, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to keep searching past the first answer, humble enough to keep learning, and excited by problems without textbook solutions.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside engineers to solve problems where milliseconds matter and better models create real competitive advantage. You'll get meaningful ownership from day one, in a culture built on intellectual honesty and continuous improvement. Your contribution won't be measured by hours spent, but by the quality of your thinking.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created. Every day, someone discovers a better answer. This summer, that someone could be you.

- Concept scoping to quickly solidify requirements

- Feature trade-off / trade tables

- Total Cost of Ownership modeling

- Joint design development, via clear statements of work

- Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs

- Complete the BOM risk assessment and develop plan per part analysis

- Follow through completion of component qualifications by relevant stakeholders, ahead of production need dates

- Reduce complexity of supply chain through commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization

- Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product lifecycle

- Manage ad-hoc cost issues e.g., tariffs / import export cost, and cost inflation

- Drive the design and implementation of new supply chain processes and systems, ensuring they meet business requirements and are built for scale

- Manage project schedules, identify critical path activities, and proactively identify and mitigate risks to keep initiatives on track

- Hold project teams and stakeholders accountable for deliverables and deadlines, navigating organizational complexity to clear roadblocks and drive decisions

Benefits

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

- No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications:

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

- Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

- What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. In this individual contributor role, you will join a cross-functional product pod: a small team working together to solve customer and business problems. You will take a problem from an early prototype to working, AI-enabled software in the hands of real users, then improve it through feedback and weekly iteration. You will have meaningful ownership, with responsibility for the quality, progress, and outcomes of your work.

We welcome experience across engineering, product, design, learning, program management, business systems, and related disciplines. Bring your professional judgment and readiness to learn. Through AI-native training, hands-on delivery, and collaboration with your pod, you will build current skills while contributing the perspective of your prior career.

About the Returnship Program

- Paid, temporary program lasting 12 weeks, with a commitment of 40 hours per week, fully onsite in Pleasanton, California

- Designed for experienced professionals returning after a career break, typically two or more years away from paid work

- Placement at Colibri’s individual contributor level IC2 or above during the program, based on prior experience, with a discipline descriptor reflecting your professional background

- Structured AI-native training and real project work, supported by manager coaching, mentorship, and peer connections

This temporary program does not include company-sponsored benefits. The program may lead to future employment in Product & Technology; conversion is not guaranteed and depends on performance, business needs, and approved headcount. Any future role and level will reflect demonstrated scope; prior level informs placement but does not guarantee it.

What You’ll Do

- Refresh your skills and apply them immediately. Complete Colibri’s AI-native training and use it in active project work, building fluency in current tools and ways of working

- Own a customer or business problem. Move from prototype through build, hardening, release, and iteration while owning the outcome and timeline within your pod’s commitments

- Deliver working software to real users. Take the fastest responsible path to a minimum viable product and then beta. Your work will reach production, beyond a local demonstration

- Apply your professional judgment. Use your prior experience to define scope, weigh trade-offs, align stakeholders, and help the pod make better decisions

- Show progress every week. Demonstrate your work in weekly demos and communicate progress, risks, and next steps clearly and honestly

- Direct and evaluate AI tools. Use AI coding and agent tools to accelerate delivery. When output falls short, identify the cause and improve the context, prompts, tools, or tests behind it

- Bring the standards of your discipline. Create strong requirements, designs, architecture, tests, learning designs, or programs, as relevant to your background, and learn how other disciplines contribute.

- Own quality. Review AI-generated and peer work for maintainability, test coverage, security, and fitness for purpose. Build quality into the work throughout delivery

- Support others and keep learning. Share your experience with early-career builders, help teammates break down and communicate work, seek feedback, and change your approach when evidence calls for it

What You’ll Bring

- Typically three or more years of prior professional experience in engineering, product, design, learning, program management, business systems, or a related field

- A career break from paid work, typically two or more years, and readiness to relaunch your career through hands-on product delivery

- Evidence of the scope you held before your break, such as products delivered, outcomes owned, or teams and stakeholders influenced

- Readiness to retrain on AI coding and agent tools, work at pace, and take responsibility for the quality of what you build

- Professional judgment, customer empathy, clear communication, and a collaborative approach to mentoring and receiving feedback

- A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent professional experience

- Availability for the full 12-week, 40-hour-per-week onsite commitment in Pleasanton, California

Preferred: Experience in professional education, edtech, ecommerce, B2B SaaS, or regulated markets.

Tools, Platforms, and Methodologies You May Use

Experience with every tool or methodology below is not required. We are most interested in your ability to learn quickly, direct AI effectively, and apply professional judgment to work that reaches real users.

- AI coding assistants and agent tools, including context development, prompting, and evaluation of AI-generated work

- Rapid prototyping, minimum viable product development, production delivery, and iterative improvement

- Discipline-specific requirements, design, architecture, testing, learning design, and program artifacts

- Weekly demonstrations, customer feedback, and cross-functional product pod collaboration

Why You’ll Love Working Here

- Relaunch with meaningful ownership. Build recent experience by delivering working software to real users and seeing how they respond

- Learn AI through practical application. Complete structured training and use those skills immediately with your pod

- Put your prior experience to work. Your judgment will help shape decisions, strengthen delivery, and support early-career colleagues

- Make an impact connected to your own journey. Help build products that advance learners’ careers while rebuilding momentum in yours

We Encourage You to Apply

You may not check every preferred box, and that is okay. We welcome experienced returners from engineering, product and design, learning, program management, and business systems. This program values transferable expertise and the ability to learn new ways of working.

You should be ready for hands-on building, accountable ownership, and the full onsite program commitment. Success will be visible in work delivered to users, weekly progress, the quality of your artifacts, how you diagnose and improve AI output, and how you respond to feedback and support your pod. If this sounds like the next step you have been looking for, we would love to hear from you.

What You Can Expect From Our Hiring Process

We want you to understand the program and the team while we learn about your experience and goals. We do not use AI to review applications; a human on our Talent Acquisition team reviews your application. While the exact process may vary, you can generally expect:

- Recruiter Conversation Discuss your background, return-to-work goals, interests, program availability, and compensation

- Hiring Manager Conversation Explore your previous scope, professional judgment, approach to learning, and potential project work

- Team and/or Cross-Functional Interviews Meet potential partners and discuss the skills and experiences most relevant to the program

- Final Conversation and Decision Some opportunities may include an additional conversation. Talent Acquisition will keep you informed about next steps and timing. We encourage your questions throughout the process

Our Commitment to Inclusion
Colibri Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome, respected, and empowered to do their best work. We encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds, experiences, and career paths to apply!!

As a Software Engineer Intern at Palantir, you’ll own every phase of the product lifecycle—from generating ideas and designing prototypes to executing features and shipping releases—while being paired with a dedicated mentor who champions your growth. Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Our Cloud Memory Business Unit defines and incubates next-generation memory and system architectures for datacenter and AI workloads. In this internship you will help develop and validate a first-principles system-modeling capability that evaluates memory-centric architectures across rack-scale AI platforms — quantifying tradeoffs before committing to silicon or full software implementations.

We are seeking a Memory & System Architecture Research Intern with a strong computer-architecture and systems-modeling background to characterize AI workloads and help build and validate performance models for advanced memory systems. You will translate AI workload trends into memory capacity, bandwidth, and latency requirements, and quantify architectural tradeoffs to inform long-term technology and product direction. This role suits a graduate or Ph.D. student who is comfortable in ambiguous problem spaces and enjoys turning hypotheses into quantified, published evidence. Applying Artificial Intelligence is expected as part of this position.

Key Responsibilities

- Workload characterization: Analyze AI training and inference workloads to derive memory bandwidth, capacity, and latency requirements.
- System modeling: Contribute to analytical and simulation models that evaluate memory-centric system architectures at scale.
- Architecture studies: Assess system-level tradeoffs across emerging memory and integration technologies.
- Validation & accuracy: Benchmark models against reference data to improve accuracy and ensure reproducible results.
- Quantified analysis: Produce system-level performance, efficiency, and cost analyses that inform architectural decisions.
- Documentation & publishing: Capture findings in internal technical reports and contribute to invention disclosures where applicable.

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently pursuing an M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Architecture, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- Strong background in computer architecture and system-level performance analysis (memory hierarchy, bandwidth, latency, scaling).
- Ability to analyze complex memory and AI performance challenges and reason about tradeoffs quantitatively.
- Proficiency in Python for building analytical models and performance analysis.
- Good verbal and written communication and problem-solving abilities.

Preferred Qualifications

- Understanding of memory architectures (HBM, DDR, LPDDR, CXL, emerging memories) and their impact on AI/ML workloads.
- Understanding of near-memory and advanced integration technologies — 3D stacking, chiplets, interposers, heterogeneous packaging — and their system-level tradeoffs.
- Experience with AI systems and accelerators (GPU/ASIC), performance benchmarking, or design-space exploration.
- Familiarity with simulation frameworks and reproducible experimentation.

What You'll Gain

Turn architecture hypotheses into quantified, published evidence that shapes next-generation memory technology and product direction, while working alongside senior memory and systems architects on some of the most challenging problems in AI infrastructure.

About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

Who we are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

What you’ll do

As an ML Intern on our team, you will help bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. Working alongside senior engineers, you will contribute directly to production-grade models, real-time edge pipelines, and multi-sensor data systems that power our physical machines.

- Collaborate with research engineers to prototype, evaluate, and test emerging Machine Learning and Deep Learning models for trajectory planning and autonomous behavior.

- Help design and evaluate multimodal systems that integrate raw multi-sensor data (Cameras, LiDAR, Radar) to improve spatial-temporal perception.

- Assist in developing interactive world models and simulation tools to re-simulate real-world driving logs and analyze vehicle trajectories.

- Profile and optimize inference pipelines to help run complex models under low latency constraints on vehicle edge hardware.

- Work with data engineering workflows to identify, curate, and structure rare, complex edge cases and long-tail scenarios from physical operations.

- Partner with validation and QA teams to run model releases through simulated scenarios to catch performance regressions and track model behavior.

What we’re looking for

- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field.

- Strong foundation in deep learning concepts and experience with modern frameworks like PyTorch or JAX (through coursework, research, or prior internships).

- Hands-on programming experience in Python; familiarity with C++ is a plus.

- Academic coursework, project experience, or research in one or more relevant domains: Computer Vision, Spatial-Temporal Modeling, Reinforcement Learning, Model Optimization, Model Evaluation, or Data Engineering.

- Familiarity with robotics data structures or multi-sensor processing (Cameras, LiDAR, or Radar) is highly preferred.

- A passion for solving complex, messy real-world engineering problems and deploying AI into physical systems.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

- Software development for real-time embedded systems written in C / C++ using OOP principles.
- Software development for embedded microcontrollers including Linux.
- Design and implementation of low power, battery operated devices.
- Hardware schematics and design/implement associated with embedded software.
- Integrating hardware and software using data buses and protocols such as SPI, I2C, RS-232, or DMA.

Job Description

The PNC CIO Quantitative Modeling team develops models and analytics for deposit behavior, mortgage products, and firm’s investment portfolio. The team applies economics, finance, and data-driven research to quantify interest rate risk, and support investment and balance sheet management decisions.

We are seeking PhD and Master's students in Economics, Finance, Econometrics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or related quantitative disciplines who are nearing graduation. This internship is designed for candidates with strong econometric and empirical research training who want to apply quantitative methods to real-world financial and economic challenges. Successful candidates will have a strong analytical background and experience conducting empirical research using economic and financial data.

This position is based in New York City and requires full-time, in-office participation.

PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position.

Job Responsibilities

As an intern, the candidate will participate in the many activities of the modeling team. These include:

- Conducting empirical research on customer behavior, fixed income markets using large financial and economic datasets.
- Developing and enhancing econometric, statistical, and predictive models for deposits, mortgage prepayments, fixed income securities, and interest rate risk measurement.
- Designing analytical frameworks that quantify balance sheet optionality and supporting portfolio and risk management decisions.
- Presenting research findings and investment insights to quantitative, risk, and business stakeholders.

- PhD (preferred) or Master's student graduating within the next 12 months.

Black Box Network Services is a leading global communications system integrator specializing in designing, sourcing, implementing, and managing complex technology solutions. As an AI Engineer Intern in the AI Center of Excellence (CoE), you will contribute to the design, development, and integration of applied AI solutions using pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs), traditional machine learning techniques, and deterministic approaches.

This role offers hands-on experience building enterprise-grade Generative AI solutions across backend services, data pipelines, orchestration, and user-facing applications. Working closely with experienced AI engineers, you will contribute to real-world AI use cases integrated with platforms such as ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and Azure services.

- Currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Engineering or a related field (Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or similar).

- Available for a full-time, on-site internship for a minimum of 6–12 months (depending on academic program constraints).

AI & Generative AI Development

- Build and integrate AI solutions using pre-trained LLMs for conversational AI, summarization, and enterprise knowledge retrieval.

- Implement RAG-based architectures connecting LLMs with structured and unstructured enterprise data.

- Develop and test AI agents, traditional ML models, and deterministic logic for real-world use cases.

Full-Stack & Enterprise Integration

- Build AI-enabled user interfaces and integrate them with backend services.

- Develop and maintain backend APIs and services.

- Integrate AI solutions with enterprise platforms such as ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and Azure services.

Data, Testing & Deployment

- Build and maintain data pipelines, including preprocessing and quality checks.

- Support testing, debugging, deployment, and monitoring of AI services on Azure.

- Document AI workflows, integrations, and solution lifecycle updates.

Learning & Collaboration

- Collaborate with AI, data, and platform teams to deliver production-ready AI solutions.

- Continuously learn and apply best practices in Generative AI, RAG patterns, and enterprise AI systems.

- Programming: Strong working knowledge of Python.

- Applied AI / GenAI: Hands-on experience building or integrating ML or Generative AI solutions.

- Generative AI: Practical experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and/or RAG-based architectures.

Description

Do you want to apply your analytical, research, data, or language skills to real-world problems and gain experience with cyber operations?

Are you excited by ambiguous problems and interested in turning research and analysis into impactful mission insight?

Are you intellectually curious, constantly seeking to understand global events, emerging threats, adversary behavior, and the relationships between them?

Are you passionate about cybersecurity, intelligence, and national security?

If these questions resonate with you, you may be a great fit for an internship with the Cyber Warfare Systems Group (QCR)! QCR team members apply their skills to offensive security operations and non-kinetic mission defeat. We help the U.S. military address complex cyber operations challenges and execute cyber missions at scale in support of joint operations. Our best solutions often emerge at the intersection of technology, intelligence, data, human behavior, and mission understanding. We bring together people with multidisciplinary analytical and mission backgrounds because the hardest cyber operations problems rarely fit neatly within a single discipline. Our research areas include analysis and targeting, cyber-layer modeling, cybersecurity, and human-systems modeling.

As a member of our team...

You will gain a hands-on analytical internship experience. Interns work alongside and learn from analysts, researchers, engineers, and cyber practitioners while contributing to real problems supporting cyber operations. Depending on your interests, background, and experience, you may:

- Investigate complex questions using open-source information, publicly or commercially available information, data, intelligence, foreign-language sources, and other research methods.
- Apply analytical methods such as intelligence analysis, targeting, graph theory, network analysis, data science, structured analytic techniques, or human-systems analysis.
- Develop assessments, analytical methods, data products, visualizations, or decision-support approaches that turn complex information into useful mission insight.
- Use and critically evaluate AI-enabled analytical tools and emerging methods, understanding both their potential and limitations.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary APL teams and government and contractor partners as analysis informs capability development and mission execution.
- Have opportunities to contribute your own ideas and perspective. Our interns are active members of the team, eager to learn quickly, and make a meaningful team impact.

Customer Experience Internship

We're Carvana. And we're on a mission to change the way people buy and sell cars.

We're a disruptor, an innovator, and a team that's obsessed with creating an unforgettable customer experience. And we believe that mission starts with our people.

That's where you come in.

About the internship: the ultimate customer operations bootcamp

Forget what you think you know about internships. This isn't your average "get coffee and make copies" gig. This is a 9-week (June 7 – August 6, 2027), paid, immersive bootcamp designed to teach you how to drive customers happy at one of the most innovative companies in business today.

You'll be embedded in our world-class Customer Experience team, learning from the ground up what it takes to deliver moments of magic to our customers. You'll also get exposure to our Market Operations team, so you can see the driveway and Vending Machine experience up close and appreciate the full, end-to-end car buying journey. Our goal is to give you a 360-degree view of that journey and empower you to make a real, tangible impact.

This is your chance to be part of a team that's making history, all while building a foundation for your future career.

We are investing in your development with the ultimate goal of you joining us full-time, so we're looking for candidates who are passionate about building their future at Carvana post-graduation.

What you'll be doing

- Learn from the best: You'll go through an accelerated training program designed to give you a deep understanding of our customers, our business, and our secret sauce for success.

- Become a customer champion: You'll be on the front lines, engaging with real customers through live interactions via phone and chat to solve problems and create exceptional experiences.

- See the full journey: Get exposure to the Market Operations side of the business and gain insight into the driveway and Vending Machine experience, so you understand how every step of the car buying process comes together.

- Experience our innovation firsthand: Step away from the desk and see what makes Carvana different. You'll get exclusive tours of our iconic Car Vending Machine and state-of-the-art Inspection Center as you learn about all the teams that bring the customer experience to life.

- Tackle a real business challenge: You and your fellow interns will team up on a hands-on capstone project, presenting your innovative solutions to our senior leadership team at the end of the summer.

- Get a seat at the table: Participate in exclusive lunch & learn sessions with our Executives, get a behind-the-scenes look at our operations, and build a professional network that will last a lifetime.

Your launchpad: where this internship can take you

At the end of the internship, full-time and part-time opportunities are available in our Advocate Operational roles, in either Customer Care or Market Operations. Those are your starting lines, not your finish line.

At Carvana, the growth doesn't stop in your first role. After 6 months, you become eligible to grow into other teams across the company. We have a ton of internal growth opportunities, and Customer Care is truly the launchpad for them. Because you've spent your time becoming the expert in the experiences we create for customers, you'll bring something every team values: a real understanding of the customer.

- Start: Join as an Advocate in Customer Care or Market Operations after graduation.

- Grow: Become eligible to move into other teams at the 6-month mark.

- Lead the way: Take the customer expertise you've built into whatever career you choose here.

What you should have

We're looking for people who are fired up about our mission and ready to learn. While we don't expect you to have any prior corporate experience, we are looking for:

- Currently enrolled in a four-year university and on track to graduate in Winter 2027 or Spring 2028 (i.e., a rising senior).

- A genuine obsession with helping people and a deep sense of empathy.

- An insatiable curiosity and a desire to understand the "why" behind the "what."

- A top-notch communicator: you're clear, concise, and can talk to just about anyone.

- A true team player who is always willing to lend a hand.

- Resilience and a positive, can-do attitude. You see challenges as opportunities.

What you'll get

- A paid, full-time 9-week internship at $20/hr.

- A pathway to a full-time Advocate Operational role in Customer Care or Market Operations, with eligibility to grow into other teams at the 6-month mark. We're not just looking for summer help; we're looking for our next generation of team members.

- A hands-on learning experience that will look amazing on your resume and serve as a launchpad for your career, whether that's with us or beyond.

- Direct mentorship and coaching from a dedicated manager and a team that is invested in your growth.

- Unparalleled access to senior leaders and cross-functional teams.

- An unforgettable summer filled with learning, development, and fun.

- And, of course, some seriously cool Carvana swag.

Interested?

If you're ready to roll up your sleeves, make a difference, and launch your career at a company that's changing the entire car-buying industry, we want to hear from you.
